criteria.criterion: backtest.rs gets each decision's start time from the git history of the decision's text in docs/decisions.md. For D87 that is the commit that introduced the entry. Only host-error and intervention records dated after that start are counted by the signals. The start time is a field of the report.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. start_from_history runs `git log --reverse --format=%cI [--first-parent] -S<heading> -- docs/decisions.md` and takes the first commit. run_signals filters observed, derived and intervention records with after_start, which is a strict `>`. Report has a new `started` field and render prints it. The test the_start_is_the_first_commit_that_added_the_entry checks that a later amendment does not move the start.

criteria.criterion: derive_host_error derives a refusal only when the text ties an HTTP code to the refused merge itself. A bare occurrence of 'merge', 'merges' or 'merged' no longer suffices. When unsure it returns None.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. names_merge is replaced by merge_refusal_status. It splits the text into clauses on . ; ? ! and line breaks. A clause qualifies only if it holds HTTP <code>, a merge word, and a refusal word or 'not allowed', and holds no opening or creating word. Otherwise the function returns None.

criteria.criterion: The backtest validates each cited record (observed host-error, derived record with its source intervention, and intervention): it matches the signal's fields and falls inside the signal's time window, meaning it postdates the decision's start. Any invalid citation adds a Finding and makes Report::passed() false. The old checks of counts and id existence remain.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. check_citations (condition e) re-reads each cited id from records. It checks that the record exists, that it matches the signal (host_error.matches or exact matches), that it falls after the start, and, for a derived record, its derived marker, its source, the source's existence, the source's time and that the dates agree. run_on calls it after the existing check_signals and check_introspection, which are unchanged. Findings make passed() false.

criteria.criterion: The citation check also covers the derived record's source intervention and the introspection record's intervention. An introspection whose triggering event predates the decision is a finding.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. check_citations checks that the source intervention exists and postdates the start. When an introspection is present, it checks the triggering intervention's existence, its time against the start ('predates the start of'), and its fields. The test a_stale_cited_record_makes_the_report_fail covers the introspection case.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`. Both pass. New tests cover: a record before the decision start is not counted; an intervention that mentions 'merged' in the sense of opening a pull request, with HTTP 422, derives nothing; a text that ties HTTP 422 or 405 to the refused merge derives a record; an invalid citation fails the backtest.
criteria.evidence: All suites passed and clippy printed no warnings. The new tests are records_before_the_decision_start_are_not_counted, opening_a_pull_request_with_a_422_derives_nothing, a_422_or_405_tied_to_the_refused_merge_derives_a_record (in both the CLI and core tests), an_invalid_citation_fails_the_backtest, a_stale_cited_record_makes_the_report_fail and the_start_is_the_first_commit_that_added_the_entry. Each would fail on the base code, where run_on and run_signals had no start parameter and names_merge matched 'merged' anywhere.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo run -- backtest` on the real records. D87 is under review citing only ar1x, both directly and through its derived record. The introspection record names ar1x's event. Nothing else is flagged. The kn3q and qk2d interventions are not cited. The actual output is reported, even if it differs.
criteria.evidence: Plain `cargo run -- backtest` fails: there are two binaries, athena and xtask. With --bin athena the run exits 2 and reads 0 jobs, 0 interventions and 0 host errors. D87 and D88 show as started 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z, because this verify tree's two synthetic commits are both dated then. Neither signal fires, and condition (b) is flagged. This tree has no records/ directory and no real git history, so the expected real result (D87 under review citing only ar1x) could not be shown. The change itself carries no measured real-records output.

findings.summary: The real-records result was not shown. Here the backtest reads no records and flags condition (b).
findings.evidence: `cargo run -q --bin athena -- backtest` printed 'records: 0 job(s)... 0 intervention(s)', 'D87 started 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z', and 'backtest: fail ... (b) the signal found 0 distinct job(s)'. `ls records` reports no such directory. Criterion 6 and the 'verified' default need the real outcome: D87 under review citing only ar1x, and kn3q and qk2d not cited. That outcome is unverified.

findings.summary: The tie between the code and the merge is approximated by the words appearing in the same clause, so some untied clauses still derive a record.
findings.evidence: A clause like 'I merged by hand because the push failed with HTTP 422' has a merge word, 'failed' and HTTP 422, and no opening word, so it would derive a 422 merge refusal although the code belongs to the push. The accepted reading allows one-clause co-occurrence, but the request asked to derive nothing when unsure.

findings.summary: The start is looked up by the current heading text, so a renamed heading would date from the rename, not from the entry's first commit.
findings.evidence: `git log -S<current heading line>` finds the first commit that contains the current heading string. If the heading's title was ever edited, that commit is the edit, not the one that introduced the entry.

findings.summary: Clause splitting on '.' also splits on decimal points and version numbers.
findings.evidence: text.split(['.', ';', '?', '!', '\n']). It is harmless for the current patterns.

summary: The change fixes all three root causes in code, and the tests cover each one. (1) A decision's start now comes from the git history of its entry (`git log -S`, first parent), and only records strictly later than it count; the start is in the report. (2) A merge refusal is derived only when one clause holds the HTTP code, a merge word and a refusal word, and no opening or creating word. (3) A new condition (e) re-checks every cited record against the signal's fields and the decision's start, including the derived record's source intervention and the introspection's triggering event. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass. The verdict is fail because the real-records result could not be shown. This tree has no records/ and only two synthetic commits dated 2000-01-01. Running the backtest here reads 0 records, puts nothing under review, and fails condition (b). So the expected outcome (D87 under review citing only ar1x, kn3q and qk2d not cited) is unverified, and the change reports no measured real-records output. There are minor concerns: same-clause co-occurrence is a loose test of the tie, and the start is looked up by the current heading text, so a renamed heading would date from the rename.
